judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Indicators (rank 1, same canonical Grade coordinate) under STRAND 4: WRITING, but in different Sub-Strands with different Content Standards: B2.4.3.1.3 'Space words appropriately in sentences' sits under 'Writing Letters – Small and Capital' (B2.4.3.1, legible/bold handwriting) while B2.4.7.1.2 'Match parts of sentences to compose meaningful texts' sits under 'Controlled Writing' (B2.4.7.1, 'Write simple compositions'). The shared object is the sentence (LC tags overlap on 'sentences'/'writing'), so they are coherent, complementary aspects of early writing—transcription/legibility mechanics alongside sentence-level composition—and they reinforce one another when pupils produce written sentences. However, the evidence shows no substantive deepening or dependency in either direction: spacing words is a handwriting presentation skill, not an established precondition for matching sentence parts for meaning, and composing texts does not extend word spacing. Same-rank placement provides no directional warrant, and the only other signals (weak code-prefix 'b2/4', weak local-rank proximity, low Jaccard token/trigram overlap driven by the substring 'sentence') are non-semantic. Source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC metadata are truncated, so a stronger developmental claim is not supportable on this bounded excerpt; the symmetric relation is what the available text supports.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 2 Content Standards (same statement-type grain, same rank 1) under STRAND 4: WRITING, but in different sub-strands: B2.4.5.1 (Sub-Strand 5: Writing Simple Words and Sentences) requires learners to 'Use knowledge of grammar and vocabulary to write words and sentences correctly', while B2.4.7.2 (Sub-Strand 7: Controlled Writing) requires 'Matching parts of sentences to composition', with the bounded source anchor showing the associated work as re-arranging jumbled sentences logically into a connected text.
